texts.facts: Complainant versus Sh. Sandeep Kumar S/o Sh Heera Lal M/s Nanu Super Stores, A-13, Krishan Vihar, Delhi - 41 R/o F-7/327, Sultan Puri, Delhi-41 ... Accused Judgment: 1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (herein after referred to as Pfa Act), alleging that the accused has violated the provisions of th e PFA Act and Rules. 2. As per the complaint, on 01.08.2003, the Food Inspector (herein after referred as FI) Sh Sanjiv Kumar Gupta purchased a sample of 'Dal Arhar' a food article for analysis from accused Sandeep DA vs Sandeep Kumar Kumar at M/s Nanu Super Stores, A-13, Krishan Vihar, Delhi - 41, where the said food article was found stored for sale and where accused No.1 Sandeep Kumar was found conducting the business of the said food article at the time of sampling. The sample consisted 1500 grams of Dal Arhar (ready for sale) taken from an open gunny bag bearing no label declaration. The sample was taken under the supervision / direction of Sh. Harish Kumar Ahuja, SDM/LHA. The sample was taken after proper mixing the sample commodity with the help of clean and dry jhaba by rotating in all possible directions clockwise anti clockwise up and down several times. The Food Inspector divided the sample then and there into three equal parts by putting into three clean and dry bottles. Each bottle was separately packed, fastened and sealed according to PFA Act and Rules. The vendor's signatures were obtained on the LHA slip and the wrapper of the sample bottles. Notice was given to accused Sandeep Kumar and the price of sample was also given to him vide Da vs Sandeep Kumar on 2 July, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179775954/ 1 vendor receipt dated 01.08.2003. Panchnama too was prepared at the spot. All the documents prepared by F.I were signed by accused Sandeep Kumar and the other witness Sh Brahma Nand, FA. Before starting sample proceeding efforts were made to join public witnesses but none came forward, as such Sh Brahma Nand FA was joined as witness. 3. One counter-part of the sample bearing LHA code No. 63/LHA/4903 was also sent to Public Analyst, Delhi in intact condition and two counter-parts were deposited with the LHA in intact condition. Public Analyst analysed the sample and found the same to be adulterated. The report of the Public Analyst is as DA vs Sandeep Kumar follows: "The sample is Adulterated because it is coloured with synthetic colouring matter viz tartarzine." 4. It is the case of the complainant that accused Sandeep Kumar was the vendor-cum-proprietor of M/s Nanu Super Stores, A-13, Krishan Vihar, Delhi - 41 at the time of sampling as such he is incharge of and responsible for day to day conduct of the business of the said shop. 5. Thereafter on completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the court on 08.12.2003 alleging violation of section 2(ia)(j)&(m) of PFA Act, 1954 and Rule 23 read with Rule 28 & 29 of PFA Rules, 1955 as punishable section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act against the accused. 6. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 08.12.2003. The accused thereafter exercised their option of analysing the counter part through CFL under section 13(2) of the PFA Act. Based on the report of the CFL as well as evidence led in pre charge evidence, charge was framed against the accused for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1) (a) PFA Act being violation of Section 2(ia)(a)(j)&(m) and Rule 23 read with Rule 28 & 29 and Rule 24 of PFA Rules, 1955, to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. DA vs Sandeep Kumar 7. At the trial, the prosecution examined three witness in support of its case i.e. PW-1 FI Sanjeev Gupta, PW-2 FA Brahamand and PW-3 SDM/LHA Sh Harish Kumar Ahuja. PW-1 and PW-2 were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings under the supervision of SDM/LHA Sh.Harish Kumar Ahuja. These witness narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample commodity of 1500 grams of "Arhar Dal" from the vendor for analysis which was lying in an open gunny bag, bearing no label declaration, dividing the sample into three equal parts by putting them into three clean and dry glass bottles, separately sealing, packing and marking the same and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses. They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex.PW-1/A, Notice Ex. PW-1/B, Panchnama Ex.PW-1/C. The vendor furnished photocopy of driving licence Ex.PW1/J. Thereafter, on 04.08.2003 one counterpart of the sample along with one copy of memo in form VII and another copy of memo in Da vs Sandeep Kumar on 2 July, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179775954/ 2 form VII in sealed deposited with PA vide receipt Ex.PW1/D and the remaining two counter parts of the sample in intact condition along with two copies of memo of Form VII in a sealed packet were deposited with LHA vide LHA Receipt Ex.PW1/E under intimation that one counterpart of the same has already been deposited with PA. Thereafter, PA Report Ex.PW1/F was received, according to which the sample was adulterated. Thereafter PW-1 FI Sanjeev Kumar Gupta further investigated the matter and sent letter Ex.PW1/H to STO Ward No. 63 and received its reply stating that no such dealer registered in this ward. After completion of DA vs Sandeep Kumar investigation, the entire case file was put before then Director PFA for obtaining his Consent. The then Director PFA granted his Consent for prosecution vide sanction order Ex.PW1/K. Thereafter, the present complaint Ex.PW1/L was filed before the Court. Then intimation letter Ex.PW1/M alongwith copy of PA Reports was sent to the accused vide postal receipt Ex.PW1/N which was received back undelivered. These witnesses were duly cross-examined by Ld. Defence Counsel. 8. Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC were recorded on 03.09.2013 wherein the accused denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. Thereafter matter was listed for defence evidence. 9. In defence, the accused examined a witness Anil Goel as DW-1 and placed on record bill Ex.DW1/A. Thereafter defence evidence was closed vide order dated 12.05.2016 and the matter was fixed for final arguments.
texts.arguments: 14. The defence taken by the accused is that he had purchased the dal from one Nihal Chand & Company, Grave Merchant and Commission Agent, 3955, Naya Bazar, Delhi -6. In order to prove this, he has called a partner from this firm Nihal Chand & DA vs Sandeep Kumar Company as a defence witness but this witness has not identified the bill Ex.DA on which the accused is relying for the purpose of benefit of warranty.
